spec.description: Read top to bottom: is it healthy, who served it, did it tell the truth, where did the time go, and are the dependencies alive. Every panel here is backed by a metric the app actually emits.

spec.title: Run p50 (NFR < 20s)
spec.description: Median end-to-end itinerary time. NFR target is under 20s. This is the typical experience, not the worst one.

spec.title: Run p95 (NFR < 45s)
spec.description: 95th percentile itinerary time. NFR is 45s. A breach here fires RunLatencyP95Breached after 10m.

spec.title: Cost / itinerary p95 (cap $0.30)
spec.description: 95th percentile spend per itinerary against the $0.30 hard cap. Reading ~0 means the local engine is serving; a jump means a paid venue took over.

spec.title: Runs / sec
spec.description: Completed planner runs per second, all statuses.

spec.title: Failure rate
spec.description: Fraction of runs that did NOT succeed. Degraded-but-honest answers still count as succeeded — see section 2 for those.

spec.title: Spend today (all venues)
spec.description: Spend so far today (UTC): every paid call - LLM legs and query embeddings, including runs that failed. Read from the Redis ledger the daily spend breaker itself uses, so it survives restarts and is exactly the number DAILY_SPEND_LIMIT_USD acts on. (Until 2026-10-01 this panel summed per-process counters, which every restart zeroes.)

spec.title: local-sglang · latency p50
spec.description: Median seconds per LLM call served by local-sglang. Run duration averages over whichever leg answered and so cannot show this.

spec.title: local-sglang · latency p95
spec.description: 95th percentile call latency on local-sglang. The first call after idle is slower on a local engine (CUDA graph warmup).

spec.title: local-sglang · calls/sec
spec.description: Successful completions per second served by local-sglang.

spec.title: local-sglang · spend since restart
spec.description: USD on local-sglang since the worker last started - a restart zeroes it; today's total is 'Spend today'. A self-hosted venue reads exactly $0 — recorded, not absent, so 'free' and 'not measured' cannot be confused.

spec.title: Which venue served, over time
spec.description: Calls per second per venue. The moment a paid leg starts climbing, a free one died — this is the earliest visible symptom of a dead engine.

spec.title: Tokens/sec by venue and direction
spec.description: Throughput split input vs output. Output tokens dominate cost on hosted venues and dominate latency on local ones.

spec.title: Itinerary outcomes
spec.description: grounded = built from retrieved POIs. degraded = the place exists but retrieval found nothing usable. not_found = geocoding failed and we said so. A rise in degraded with no rise in errors IS silent quality loss.

spec.title: POIs returned per retrieval
spec.description: How much grounding material each query actually got. A p50 falling toward 0 means the corpus or Overpass is failing, and the itineraries above it are being written from far less evidence than they look like they have.

spec.title: Rate limiting by scope
spec.description: Refusals per scope. tenant_min bounds burst, tenant_day is the budget, ip_min closes the cookie-rotation hole. A 429 here is enforcement working, not an outage.

spec.title: API dispatch outcomes
spec.description: queued = accepted. rate_limited = refused by a limit. disabled = the kill switch or spend breaker refused it.

spec.title: Stage latency p95
spec.description: Per-stage 95th percentile: geocode -> gather -> compose -> critic. Recorded even when a stage RAISES, so a stage that fails slowly cannot look instantaneous.

spec.title: End-to-end percentiles vs NFR
spec.description: The three NFR percentiles on one axis. Note these mix venues: a local engine and Groq have different physics, so read section 1 alongside.

spec.title: Cache hit rate
spec.description: Hits over hits+misses. 'skipped' is excluded on purpose — those are breaker-open calls that never asked Redis, and counting them as misses would make a Redis outage look like a cold cache.

spec.title: Cache events by tool
spec.description: hit / miss / skipped / error per tool. A rise in 'skipped' means the Redis breaker is open and every lookup is bypassing the cache.

spec.title: Critic corrections
spec.description: How often the critic sent an itinerary back for a rewrite. Zero forever is suspicious — it usually means the critic is not running, not that the model is perfect.

spec.title: Serving venue circuit breakers
spec.description: 0 = closed (healthy), 1 = half-open (one probe admitted), 2 = open (leg skipped). A venue stuck at 2 is a leg you think you have and do not.

spec.title: Errors by type
spec.description: llm_transient = a leg failed and the chain fell through (normal during failover). llm_timeout = the venue exceeded its budget. llm_non_retryable = OUR bad request, which fails identically everywhere and is never the venue's fault.

spec.title: Runs by status
spec.description: Terminal run states. Compare with section 2: a run can succeed while producing a degraded itinerary.

spec.title: Spend by venue since restart
spec.description: Money, by venue, since process start. The line that matters is a paid venue climbing while a free one is supposed to be serving.

spec.title: embeddings · tokens since restart
spec.description: Query-embedding tokens since the worker last started. Every plan embeds its query once to search the curated corpus - even when SGLang writes the plan.

spec.title: embeddings · spend since restart
spec.description: Query-embedding spend (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, or Voyage when VOYAGE_API_KEY is set) since the worker last started. Not an LLM venue, so row 1.4 (openai chat) never showed it. It is why a 'local' plan is not exactly $0. Six decimals: one query costs about $0.000001, which four decimals would show as $0.0000.

spec.title: 0 — Is the service healthy right now?
1 — Which venue is actually answering, and what does it cost?
2 — Is the product refusing what it must?
3 — Where does the time actually go?
4 — Are the parts underneath still healthy?
